http/negotiation#

Content negotiation (RFC 9110 §12): Accept, Accept-Encoding, Accept-Charset and Accept-Language.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let accepted = AcceptedMediaTypes(request::Head::headers.text("Accept"));
let type = accepted.preference([HttpMediaType("application/json"), HttpMediaType("text/html")]);

AcceptedContentCodings("gzip;q=0.8, br").preference([ContentCoding("gzip"), ContentCoding("br")]);  // br
AcceptedLanguages("de-CH, de;q=0.9, en;q=0.5").preference(locales);
Quality(0.5.rat()).string();                                                                    // "0.5"

Description#

Content negotiation (RFC 9110 §12): Accept, Accept-Encoding, Accept-Charset and Accept-Language.

An absent field accepts everything; a field sent empty accepts nothing (but identity for codings). The most specific media range decides the quality of a type; ties go to what the client listed first. Nothing here knows which codecs or charsets exist: the caller says what is available. Fields are bounded (8192 bytes and 128 entries by default).

object Quality#

object Quality does Comparing<Quality>

Canonical exact thousandths. Rational input is validated, never rounded to a nearby legal HTTP preference. Both comparison and rendering use this grid.

object WeightedValue#

object WeightedValue

The common weighted token preserves spelling. Case, wildcards, missing-field defaults and specificity belong to field profiles; this is not a negotiation manager or codec capability. Media ranges need their own represented entity.

object AcceptedContentCodings#

object AcceptedContentCodings

A pure Accept-Encoding policy. Absent/empty are different; no coding is available just because its name appears in the client's preference field.

AcceptedContentCodings.AcceptedContentCodings#

AcceptedContentCodings()

No Accept-Encoding field: every coding is acceptable.

AcceptedContentCodings.AcceptedContentCodings#

AcceptedContentCodings(origin is string)

Reads origin within the default limits; InvalidNegotiation for text that is not the field.

AcceptedContentCodings.AcceptedContentCodings#

AcceptedContentCodings(origin is string, limits is NegotiationLimits)

Reads origin within limits.

AcceptedContentCodings.present#

present() is bool

Whether the field was sent.

AcceptedContentCodings.values#

values() is Sequencing<WeightedValue>

The entries, in order.

AcceptedContentCodings.string#

string() is string

The field as it would be written.

AcceptedContentCodings.quality#

quality(coding is ContentCoding) is Quality

How much the client wants this coding; 0 when it is not acceptable. identity stays acceptable unless excluded.

AcceptedContentCodings.preference#

preference(available is Sequencing<ContentCoding>) is ContentCoding

The coding of available the client prefers most, earlier entries winning ties; NoAcceptableValue when none is acceptable.

object AcceptedCharsets#
